correctness.rationale: Writing \(x=\cos(2\pi r/N)\) turns the sampled polynomial into \(1+ax+b(2x^2-1)\). The two adjacent cosine samples straddling \(-1/\sqrt2\) have opposite signs for \(2x^2-1\). A positive linear combination of their feasibility inequalities cancels \(b\) and gives \(a\le-2(u+v)/(1+2uv)\); choosing \(b=(1+2uv)^{-1}\) factors the candidate as \(2(x-u)(x-v)/(1+2uv)\), which is nonnegative on the sample grid because no sample lies between adjacent \(u,v\). The \(8\mid N\) contact and the \(\sqrt2\) limit follow exactly. Fresh direct feasibility checks on representative moduli \(5,6,7,8,9,16,31\) reproduced the formula. The universal claim rests on the analytic adjacent-sample argument, not the finite verifier.
